Senses.Explanation: Literally, "ten oxen." As a Chan title and label, it denotes Liangshan Kuoan's ordered set of ox-herding verses and the pictures made from them. A collection titles the work "Liangshan Kuoan Ze's Ten-Ox Verses" (梁山廓庵則和尚十牛頌); another record says, "our school has the account of herding the ox, and Liangshan has the verses on the Ten Oxen" (我宗門有牧牛之說，梁山有十牛之頌). The sequence begins with named sections including "seeking the ox" (尋牛) and "seeing the tracks" (見跡). The corpus also records direct criticism of its later handling: Baichi calls Liangshan's verses "compassionate, talk that descends into the weeds" (慈悲之故，落草之談), says later people "made a wrong move and then painted these Ten-Ox forms" (錯下手腳，更畫此十牛樣子), and urges burning them. In an encounter, a teacher interrupts a monk asked to recite the verses and asks, "Where is the ox?" (牛在甚麼處). The deviation from an ordinary count of cattle is documentary: "the Ten Oxen" (十牛) functions as the proper name of a Chan verse-and-picture series, circulated, recited, questioned, and criticized inside the record.
Senses.Note: Attested 33 times in 18 allowlisted texts. The title/series is primary and all curated occurrences concern that same work. Ordinary mentions of ten literal cattle, if encountered, would be a different thing, but the harvested allowlisted evidence did not establish such a second sense for this entry.
